prompt: Generate a third ONE-CANVAS MASTER PIXEL-ART SPRITE SHEET for Cooper, preserving one identical character design across portrait, battle, and overworld areas. Reference the real dog photos and the two actual green object photos. The green object must be understood as a dark emerald green, soft, inflated tubular loop with white repeating swirl print: chunky, rounded, fabric-covered, flexible, and toy-like. Do not turn it into a neckerchief, flat scarf, plain collar, rope, or generic green accessory. Use a single large extraction canvas with three panels: LEFT portrait panel with 12 emotion cells; TOP-RIGHT battle panel with 12 cells, mostly upright two-legged or seated-upright RPG poses and a few quadruped attacks; BOTTOM-RIGHT overworld panel with 16 cells in four strict rows north, south, east, west and four walk phases each. Battle concepts include upright guard, defensive brace, bite, gnaw, tubular-loop lasso, loop swing, toy sword, toy knuckle-duster, wind-up, follow-through, damage, defiance, victory, and tired resolve. Portrait emotions include simple, shy, anxious, shocked, helpless, sad, angry, defiant, determined, relieved, proud, and brave. Keep the dog’s black/grey/warm cream shaggy coat, cream muzzle and paws, floppy ears, expressive eyes, curled tail, and accessory consistent in every cell. Actual pixel-art input sheet, not concept art: discrete square pixel clusters, hard nearest-neighbour edges, limited warm late-SNES palette, no antialiasing, blur, photorealism, painterly gradients, text, labels, UI, scenery, or decorative framing. Leave enough separation between cells for later extraction.
